Welcome to Weald Community Primary School
"In our school, we smile, share, and shine together. Through character, we learn to think for ourselves, help each other, and grow into kind, confident people. Everyone belongs, everyone matters, and together we make our school a happy place to be."
Welcome
Ofsted wrote something which really captures the heart of our school, a quote that sums us up beautifully:
“Pupils are very proud members of this welcoming and inclusive school that is at the heart of its community. Reflecting the views of many, one pupil said, ‘We are like one big family.’ There are warm and nurturing relationships between staff and pupils. Pupils feel safe. They play happily at social times and enjoy the opportunity to play with others across the school.”
We are one of the few small village schools still holding onto that deep-rooted sense of community. Not just a school — we’re a family, and a big part of Weald village life.
From taking part in the village fête, to using the green for sports day, to singing for local residents at Christmas — we’re involved. We attend the church three times a year, even though we’re not a church school, because we believe in being part of something bigger than ourselves.

pageCache.pageTitle: Weald Community Primary School - Badgers - Year 5
pageCache.text:
Badgers - Year 5
This term in Literacy we will be exploring the fun and atmospheric Gothic novel Goth Girl and the Ghost of a Mouse; whilst losing ourselves around a Gothic mansion and estate we’ll be studying adverbs of possibility and relative clauses, as well as brushing up on our punctuation knowledge. Then we’ll explore exciting destinations around the world through a range of travel writing.
In Maths we’ll be stretching our number knowledge as we work on numbers up to 1,000,000, understanding their place value. Then we’ll practise adding and subtracting numbers with more than four digits.
In History we’ll explore how a pile of dragon bones helped solve an ancient Chinese mystery. In Art we’ll be taking a look at traditional Chinese brush painting and working on producing our own art in the same style. In Science we’ll be extending our knowledge of forces as we look at the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction. In PE the children will be developing their basketball skills at Sevenoaks School and then back at Weald they will be continuing to hone their hockey skills.
These are just a few of the highlights of the children's learning in Year 5 this term.

pageCache.pageTitle: Weald Community Primary School - Little Learners - Groups, Sessions and support (Pre-school age)
pageCache.text:
Little Learners - Groups, Sessions and support (Pre-school age)
Little Learners is a collection of welcoming activities, groups and outreach opportunities offered by Weald Community Primary School for babies, toddlers, pre‑school children and their families / carers. These sessions give children the chance to play, explore and learn in a relaxed environment, while helping families feel connected to our school community from an early age.
At Weald, we are proud of our caring, family‑like ethos and our strong links with the local community. Little Learners sessions, including activities such as Toddler Tuesday and childcare outreach, provide friendly spaces where children can develop early communication, social skills and confidence through play, and where parents and carers can meet others and build supportive relationships.
Our approach reflects our belief in developing the whole child. Through shared experiences, positive interactions and play‑based learning, children begin to build independence, curiosity and character qualities that support their journey towards nursery and school life.
Little Learners helps children and families feel welcomed, supported and familiar with Weald Community Primary School, creating strong foundations for a happy and confident start to school.
Our School

pageCache.pageTitle: Weald Community Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
At Weald Community Primary School, our Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) curriculum is shaped by our whole school vision: “In our school, we smile, share and shine together. Through character, we learn to think for ourselves, help each other, and grow into kind, confident people. Everyone belongs, everyone matters, and together we make our school a happy place to be.”
We believe that learning a foreign language opens doors to the wider world and empowers our pupils to become confident, curious and compassionate global citizens. In MFL, we smile as we enjoy new sounds and cultures, we share language and experiences with one another, and we shine by developing the communication skills needed for an ever-changing world.
Our MFL curriculum promotes independence, resilience, and collaboration. Through engaging teaching, children learn to think for themselves, make connections across languages, and develop strategies that help them understand and communicate with others. By exploring diverse cultures, pupils learn to appreciate difference, celebrate diversity, and show kindness and respect—helping each other grow into thoughtful, confident young people. MFL helps every child feel that they belong in a multicultural world, and that they matter as a learner and as a global citizen.
In line with the National Curriculum for Primary Schools, our MFL provision ensures that all pupils:
We aim to foster a lifelong love of languages by providing rich, meaningful and enjoyable learning experiences. Through songs, stories, conversation and cultural exploration, children build the skills and enthusiasm to continue learning languages beyond primary school.
Ultimately, our MFL vision is to ensure that every child at Weald Community Primary School grows into a kind, confident communicator, ready to play their part in a diverse and connected world—truly smiling, sharing and shining together.

PTA Quiz Night
PTA Quiz Night on Friday 28th February
The PTA are holding a Quiz Night on Friday 28th February at 7 p.m, for all parents, staff, family and friends. Come along for a fun evening, meet new people and support the school!
Tickets are £10 per person. We have limited places in the school hall, 6–8 people per team. Don't worry if you don't have a team, we can match you up.
We will provide table snacks. Please bring your own drinks and glasses.
Please contact the school office to make payment & reserve your place/table.

pageCache.pageTitle: Weald Community Primary School - Forest School/Outdoor Learning
pageCache.text:
Forest School/Outdoor Learning
At Weald we are fortunate in having a designated forest school area and outdoor classroom on site. This includes a fire area, trails, planters, willow walk and various other stimulating woodland environments.
Forest School is a child-centred inspirational learning process, that offers opportunities for holistic growth through regular sessions. It is a long-term programme that supports character development through play, exploration and supported risk taking. It develops confidence and self-esteem through learner inspired, hands-on experiences in a natural setting.

Parents
At Weald Community Primary School, we believe that the partnership between school and parents is vital to every child’s success and wellbeing. When we work closely together, we create a strong, supportive community that reflects our vision: In our school, we smile, share, and shine together.
Parents and carers play an essential role in nurturing the character, confidence, and kindness that we value so deeply. By maintaining open communication, celebrating achievements, and supporting learning at home, families help children learn to think for themselves, help one another, and grow into compassionate, resilient individuals.
In our community, everyone belongs and everyone matters. A positive, trusting relationship with parents ensures that every child feels known, valued, and encouraged. Together—families, staff, and pupils—we make Weald Community Primary School a happy place to be, where every child can truly shine.

Science
At Weald Community Primary School, our Science curriculum plays a vital role in helping pupils grow into independent, confident, and compassionate learners. Guided by our vision, we view Science as a powerful subject that nurtures children’s ability to think for themselves, make informed decisions, and explore the world with curiosity and joy.
In Science, children are encouraged to investigate, question, and problem solve. These experiences strengthen their ability to reason independently while also recognising the value of working together. Through shared experiments, respectful discussion, and collaborative enquiry, pupils live out our values: we smile, share, and shine together.
Scientific learning at Weald helps pupils build character. They learn to persevere when challenges arise, to listen to others’ ideas, and to approach the world with both confidence and kindness. By exploring real phenomena and asking their own questions, pupils discover how their actions and ideas matter — reinforcing our commitment that everyone belongs and everyone matters.
Ultimately, Science education at Weald empowers children to see themselves as capable, curious individuals who can shape their world. It supports them not only in understanding scientific concepts but also in becoming thoughtful, responsible, and independent people — helping to make our school a happy place where every child can shine.

pageCache.text:
Sports Premium report
About the PE and sport premium
Now in its twelfth year, the PE and sport premium helps schools provide equal access to high-quality PE, sport, and physical activity. The funding is intended to remove barriers so that all children, whatever their background or ability, can achieve and thrive.
At Weald we are proud of the opportunities that we give to our pupils in sport, whether this is the equipment in the playground or the opportunities to be taken out of school for competitions, or extra development in PE, we would like every child to be enthused in sport and use the opportunities at primary school to help develop a love for physical activity and hopefully take this up beyond school. The range of sports and clubs that we take part in and are able to travel to, is partly thanks to the money we receive from the sports premium.
Every child and young person should be supported to take part in daily physical activity. Current recommendations are at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity each day – or a minimum of 20 minutes a day for disabled children and young people.
It is important that schools make the most effective use of the PE and Sport Premium funding. To achieve this, spending should focus on improvements in five key areas:
Increased confidence, knowledge and skills of all staff in teaching PE and sport
Engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity
The profile of PE and sport is raised across the school as a tool for whole-school improvement
Broader experience of a range of sports and physical activities offered to all pupils
Increased participation in competitive sport.

pageCache.pageTitle: Weald Community Primary School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
At Weald Community Primary School, we are highly committed to our broad and creative curriculum which, we believe, exceeds the expectations of the National Primary Curriculum, 2014 and provides solid foundations for ‘life-long learning’. It is underpinned by Character Education and driven by the values of ‘Optimism’, ‘Ambition’ and ‘Respect’. The medium-term plans (detailed under ‘EYFS’ and ‘KS1/KS2’) and Subject Policies, Action Plans, Assessment and Progression Frameworks, place an emphasis on a cross-curricular and enquiry-based approach so that children learn more holistically and become more accountable for their own progress and attainment.
Please see the curriculum statement 2025
Their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development is nurtured throughout the curriculum; of particular importance in this regard is the influence of Character Education.
For more details on our Character Education programme, please see our summary of character education
The content of the curriculum followed in each academic year for every subject can be found on the designated pages for EYFS, KS1 & KS2. The Long Term Overview provides the structure of learning and teaching for the entire academic year whilst the Medium Term Plans (issued six times per year) are more detailed outlines of curriculum content. For more detail, please see link to The National Curriculum
In terms of phonics, reading and writing provision, Read, write, Inc is used throughout the school, supported by the Read, Write, Inc Spelling Scheme and book bag scheme.
